text.p: Here are highlights from Swiss newspapers on Friday:
- Swiss lower house of parliament voted against an initiative to restrict research in the field of genetic technology.
- Zurich Insurance Group reported a 32.7 percent increase in net profits for the first semester of 1996.
- Two Swiss chemical giants Sandoz and Ciba said that they will raise wages by 1.3 percent next year.
- Former president of the Swiss National Bank, Markus Lusser, has been elected chairman of the Swiss J. P. Morgan subsidiary.
- Swiss Federal Rail presented its first two-level rail coaches for Intercity trains on Thursday.
- The U.S. Federal Appellate Court confirmed a ruling against Sulzer subsidiary Intermedics, which was fined $73 million for violating a patent of U.S. competitor Stryker.

- Glueckskette, one of the most successful charity institutions in Switzerland, celebrated its 50th anniversary on Thursday in Berne, raising money for educational projects in the third world and for disadvantaged people in Switzerland.
- Swiss National Bank lowered the discount rate by half a percentage point to 1.0 percent.
- Swissair employees in France went on a one day strike on Thursday to protest against Swissair's plans to axe 66 jobs.
